Shot hole borer - Tree begins declining from the top down, may begin at the middle. There is no tree currently, but a cal state uni is close to a treatment.

Asian bark beetle - Mostly affects pine trees, you'll see the canopy begin to die off. Water the tree extensively, providing nutrients as required by region. Trees can survive this if diseased.

Fire blight - individual limbs dying off, slow to affect tree. Newly Budden leaves geow, then turn bright red. Most prelevant in pear trees. This is transmitted to each tree by failing to sanitize your pruning equipment between trees. There is no cure, but it is a slow moving disease.

oh, you're at work? Yeah, it's probably filtered. Strange that it's not indicated - that suggests they're not using a web-filter package, which also suggests IT is legit. Presuming this is windows, do a tracert. Open a command prompt (Start - cmd) and type "tracert imgoat.com" - it will list each system that it hits on the way to the website. There are typically 12-15. The first thing you hit should be your network gateway, if it doesn't get past that it's clearly blocked on your network. If it does, it should start hitting ISP servers (roadrunner, level3, etc). At that point it's outside the building and maybe your ISP is fucked. To get around work-based filtering just install a remote access tool on your home pc and remote into it. All of your browsing now occurs on your own computer and they can only see that you opened a remote session of some kind. Really the best way to go in snoopy/stiff networks environments.
